fact: Sao Tome and Principe's Cadastro Social Unico, set up by Decreto-Lei 16/2018 and regulated by Decreto-Lei 3/2023, was expanded by a data update from 8,000 to more than 12,500 households, the prime minister said (RSTP).
The Direcao da Protecao Social says about 12,500 households, 25% of the population, are registered in the Cadastro Social Unico, a system built to identify and target support to vulnerable families.
The DPSSF reports it updated 12,560 households and 52,808 individuals in the Cadastro Social Unico in a 2026 recertification and expansion from 8,000 to 12,000 households.
The Labour Minister said on 27 January 2026 that the Cadastro Social Único system already works and is being improved from eight thousand to twelve thousand households.
The World Bank project paper says São Tomé and Príncipe's Unique Social Registry was launched in 2024 and holds data on 8,740 families, about 16% of the national population.
